messages:
support_ana: :rotating_light: Hey team — multiple customers (3 separate tenants) have reported 5xx errors from the hosted API (/v1/generate) starting ~2026-03-15T10:04:00-07:00. Errors look like gateway/control-plane deps failing. Pasting first customer repro and a couple logs below. Can eng-oncall pick this up?

oncall_mike: on it. I see alerts from infra-alerts too. What errors are customers seeing? Request IDs?

support_ana: customers see `502` or `504` depending on request. One example: request id `req_0a1b2c3d` from tenant alpha. They get: 

```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
{
  "error": "control-plane: auth/session-service: 500 internal"
}
```

And another tenant beta: 
```
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
{
  "error": "control-plane: config-db: read timeout"
}
```

support_ana: Repro curl we gave customer (works intermittently):

```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwoodai.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-16k","input":"test"}' \
  -v
```

oncall_mike: Thanks. I pulled traces for those request IDs — control-plane call to `session-validate` returned 500 with stack: `java.sql.SQLTransientConnectionException: Timeout waiting for connection from pool` in config-db connector. Routing policy service also returned 503 for some requests. Suspect config DB connections exhausted.

raj_sre: +1, saw same on metrics — connection pool saturation on config-db read cluster around 10:03. CPU & net look normal on app nodes. There was a config push earlier today from product that increased routing policy rule complexity (large JSON arrays). Could be query cost spike.

jen_runtime: If routing-policy lookups are slow, the control plane times out and the gateway responds 502/504. We have circuit breakers but maybe thresholds too high. Quick mitigation: enable `policy-cache` TTL and fallback to default routing for affected tenants. I can flip the runtime flag if we agree.

claire_prod: That config push was a rollout to 40% canary at 09:50 for new multi-tenant rules. We didn't expect query explosion. Rolling back is an option but will impact customers using the new rules.

oncall_mike: Immediate plan: 1) enable policy-cache TTL (jen) 2) scale config-db read pool by +2 replicas (raj/infra) 3) temporarily lower circuit breaker to fail fast at gateway to return 5xx quickly rather than stall (mike) 4) notify customers with ETA.

raj_sre: Infra: provisioning read replica now. ETA ~6 mins. Also increasing DB connection pool max for proxy layer from 80->120 as a stopgap.

jen_runtime: I'm toggling `policy-cache:enable=true` and increasing TTL to 5m for routing-policy service now. Command: `POST /admin/flags` body `{ "policy_cache": {"enabled":true, "ttl_s":300}}`. Will monitor.

ops-bot: [config-change] user=jen_runtime flag=policy_cache enabled ttl_s=300 status=ok ts=1771234580

infra-alerts: Detected reduction in 5xx rate after config change: 5xx spike down from 12/min -> 2/min. Config-db connection usage trending down.

support_ana: Customers report fewer errors now for alpha and beta. One tenant still seeing intermittent 502s (req `req_7f9e2`).

raj_sre: We still have a hot shard on config-db for the tenant gamma — slow queries from routing-policy. I captured the slow SQL: `SELECT rules FROM routing_rules WHERE tenant_id = ?` with a 7s execution. Query plan shows missing index on tenant_id + rule_version. Adding composite index will fix but takes a few mins to apply. I'll run with low priority.

claire_prod: Given rollback impact, prefer patching DB + keep cache on. If index works, we can resume canary.

oncall_mike: Agreed. Raj — apply index with online algorithm, low priority. Jen — keep cache enabled and watch for stale behavior. I'll prepare customer note: ETA 30 mins for full recovery.

raj_sre: Index applied (online). Verified query times down to ~20ms. Confirming metrics: config-db latency back to baseline.

ops-bot: [db-migration] migration=add_index_routing_rules user=raj_sre status=ok ts=1771234612

jen_runtime: Routing-policy errors went to 0 in last 2m. Circuits stabilized. Keeping cache TTL for 1h to be safe.

oncall_mike: Sending update to affected customers now. Severity P2 -> will convert to postmortem follow-up.

support_ana: Thanks everyone. Customers acknowledged and on the follow-up thread asked for root cause details. I'll include this timeline and actions. Please add notes for postmortem: the canary config introduced heavy routing queries, config-db pool exhaustion, missing index, policy-cache disabled by default. Action items: update rollout checklist to include DB query-cost review, enable policy-cache for heavy rules, add automated index suggestions from slow query logs.

claire_prod: I'll add checklist item and pause canary resume until we have regression test for routing-policy load.

raj_sre: I'll open infra ticket to increase config-db pool autoscaling and add slow-query alert thresholds.

oncall_mike: Closing thread when we have postmortem doc link. Nice work. :thumbsup:
